arxiv-1506-00121.title: Studying color connection effects of e + ​ e − → c ​ c ¯ ​ c ​ c ¯ → Ξ c ​ c + X e^{+}e^{-}\to c\bar{c}c\bar{c}\to\Xi_{cc}+X process within Quark Combination Model
arxiv-1506-00121.creator: Y. Jin, H. L. Li, S. Q. Li, S. Y. Li, Z. G. Si, T. Yao, X. F. Zhang
arxiv-1506-00121.description: Abstract The color connection of the parton system is an important bridge to connect the perturbative process and the hadronization one. The special color connection of four-heavy-quark system in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} annihilation, which is the necessary one for the doubly heavy baryon and tetraquark productions is revisited.

arxiv-2011-14973.description: Abstract . In this paper, we first show that a complete shrinking breather with Ricci curvature bounded from below must be a shrinking gradient Ricci soliton. This result has several applications. First, we can classify all complete 3 3 -dimensional shrinking breathers.

arxiv-2208-12401.title: Scalable Set Encoding with Universal Mini-Batch Consistency and Unbiased Full Set Gradient Approximation
arxiv-2208-12401.creator: Jeffrey Willette, Seanie Lee, Bruno Andreis, Kenji Kawaguchi, Juho Lee, Sung Ju Hwang
arxiv-2208-12401.description: Abstract Recent work on mini-batch consistency (MBC) for set functions has brought attention to the need for sequentially processing and aggregating chunks of a partitioned set while guaranteeing the same output for all partitions. However, existing constraints on MBC architectures lead to models with limited expressive power.

arxiv-2211-04404.title: An Energy-Based Lengthscale for Reduced Order Models of Turbulent Flows Journal: arXiv.org
arxiv-2211-04404.creator: Changhong Mou, Elia Merzari, Omer San, Traian Iliescu
arxiv-2211-04404.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel reduced order model (ROM) lengthscale that is constructed by using energy distribution arguments. The new energy-based ROM lengthscale is fundamentally different from the current ROM lengthscales, which are built by using dimensional arguments.

arxiv-2305-10780.title: Dark matter condensates as highly nonlocal solitons: instability in the Schwarzschild metric and laboratory analog
arxiv-2305-10780.creator: Ludovica Dieli, Claudio Conti
arxiv-2305-10780.description: Abstract Theories on the bosonic nature of dark matter are a promising alternative to the cold dark matter model. Here we consider a dark matter halo in the state of a Bose-Einstein condensate, subject to the gravitation of a black hole.

arxiv-2501-10056.title: Symmetry-adapted closest Wannier modeling based on complete multipole basis set
arxiv-2501-10056.creator: Rikuto Oiwa 1 , Akane Inda 2 , Satoru Hayami 2 , Takuya Nomoto 3 , Ryotaro Arita 1,4 , and Hiroaki Kusunose 5
arxiv-2501-10056.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rikuto Oiwa 1 , Akane Inda 2 , Satoru Hayami 2 , Takuya Nomoto 3 , Ryotaro Arita 1,4 , and Hiroaki Kusunose 5. We have developed a method to construct a symmetry-adapted Wannier tight-binding model based on the closest Wannier formalism and the symmetry-adapted multipole theory.

arxiv-2512-07885.title: ByteStorm: a multi-step data-driven approach for Tropical Cyclones detection and tracking
arxiv-2512-07885.creator: Davide Donno, Donatello Elia, Gabriele Accarino, Marco De Carlo, Enrico Scoccimarro, Silvio Gualdi
arxiv-2512-07885.description: Abstract Accurate tropical cyclones (TCs) tracking represents a critical challenge in the context of weather and climate science. Traditional tracking schemes mainly rely on subjective thresholds, which may introduce biases in their skills on the geographical region of application. We present ByteStorm , an efficient data-driven framework for reconstructing TC tracks without threshold tuning.

arxiv-2602-23270.title: Dyson spheres on H–R diagram
arxiv-2602-23270.creator: Amirnezam Amiri
arxiv-2602-23270.description: Abstract The construction of Dyson spheres, megastructures designed to capture the total radiative output of stars, can be one of the most compelling techno-signature scenarios for advanced extraterrestrial civilizations. By considering equilibrium temperatures, we investigate the luminosities and fluxes of Dyson spheres built around two promising classes of host stars: white dwarfs and red M-dwarfs.

pmc-10563354.title: Dynamics of depressive states among university students in Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic: an interrupted time series analysis
pmc-10563354.creator: N Shiraishi, M Sakata, R Toyomoto, K Yoshida, Y Luo, Y Nakagami, A Tajika, T Watanabe, E Sahker, T Uwatoko, T Shimamoto, T Iwami, T A Furukawa
pmc-10563354.description: BackgroundThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic was reported to have increased depression among university students which was associated with impairments in their campus lives. This study examined changes in depressive states among Japanese university students during the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsA secondary data analysis from a factorial randomized controlled trial involving smartphone-based cognitive-behavioral therapy was performed.

pmc-11332948.title: Regional characterization of meteorological and agricultural drought in Baluchistan province, Pakistan
pmc-11332948.creator: Muhammad Rafiq, Yue Cong Li, Ghani Rahman, Khawar Sohail, Kamil Khan, Aun Zahoor, Farrukh Gujjar, Hyun-Han Kwon, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam, Salim Heddam
pmc-11332948.description: Drought is a complex natural hazard that occurs when a region experiences a prolonged period of dry conditions, leading to water scarcity and negative impacts on the environment. This study analyzed the recurrence of drought and wet spells in Baluchistan province, Pakistan.

pmc-11343746.title: Twin support vector regression for characterizing uncertainty in surface reconstruction
pmc-11343746.creator: ShiCheng Yu, JiaQing Miao, FeiLong Qin
pmc-11343746.description: Surface reconstruction plays a pivotal role in various fields, including reverse engineering, and oil and gas exploration. However, errors in available data and insufficient surface morphology information often introduce uncertainty into the reconstruction. It is crucial to accurately characterize and visualize the uncertainty in surface reconstruction for risk analysis and planning further data collection.

pmc-11511291.title: Structures of the Varicella Zoster Virus Glycoprotein E and Epitope Mapping of Vaccine-Elicited Antibodies
pmc-11511291.creator: Wayne D Harshbarger, Genevieve Holzapfel, Nishat Seraj, Sai Tian, Chelsy Chesterman, Zongming Fu, Yan Pan, Claire Harelson, Dongjun Peng, Ying Huang, Sumana Chandramouli, Enrico Malito, Matthew James Bottomley, James Williams, Toshi Nagata
pmc-11511291.description: Background: Varicella zoster virus (VZV) is the causative agent for chickenpox and herpes zoster (HZ, shingles). HZ is a debilitating disease affecting elderly and immunocompromised populations. Glycoprotein E (gE) is indispensable for viral replication and cell-to-cell spread and is the primary target for anti-VZV antibodies.

pmc-11532050.title: Blocking S100A9-signaling is detrimental to the initiation of anti-tumor immunity
pmc-11532050.creator: Melike Fusun Demir, Yu-Hsien Lin, Pedro Henrique Costa Cruz, Masaki Tajima, Tasuku Honjo, Elisabeth Müller
pmc-11532050.description: S100A9, a multifunctional protein mainly expressed by neutrophils and monocytes, poses an immunological paradox. In virus infections or sterile inflammation, it functions as an alarmin attracting innate immune cells, as well as mediating proinflammatory effects through TLR4 signaling. However, in cancer, S100A9 levels have been shown to associate with poor prognosis and lack of response to immunotherapy.

pmc-11592535.title: Primary Stability of Zirconia Dental Implants with Cylindrical and Tapered Designs Across Varying Bone Densities: An In Vitro Evaluation
pmc-11592535.creator: Diogo Fernandes, Francisco Cavaco, Filipe Freitas, Duarte Marques, João Caramês, André Moreira
pmc-11592535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: While titanium implants are widely recognized for their clinical success, zirconia implants have emerged as a metal-free alternative. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of zirconia implant macrogeometry and bone density on primary implant stability. Methods: Two types of zirconia implants were tested—the Neodent® Zi Ceramic Implant and the Straumann® PURE Ceramic Implant, that were placed into polyurethane foam blocks mimicking different bone densities (10 PCF, 15 PCF, 20 PCF, 30 PCF, and 40 PCF).

pmc-11753174.title: Development of the brain network control theory and its implications
pmc-11753174.creator: Zhoukang Wu, Liangjiecheng Huang, Min Wang, Xiaosong He
pmc-11753174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Brain network control theory (NCT) is a groundbreaking field in neuroscience that employs system engineering and cybernetics principles to elucidate and manipulate brain dynamics. This review examined the development and applications of NCT over the past decade. We highlighted how NCT has been effectively utilized to model brain dynamics, offering new insights into cognitive control, brain development, the pathophysiology of neurological and psychiatric disorders, and neuromodulation. Additionally, we summarized the practical implementation of NCT using the nctpy package.

pmc-13021363.title: Apoptotic periodontal ligament stem cells combined with developmental endothelial locus-1 counteract experimental periodontitis with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-13021363.creator: Qian Ma, Houxuan Li, Xiaoyu Yang, He Wang, Yiyao Hu, Han Li, Deping Zeng, Jie Li, Jinlin Song
pmc-13021363.description: Stem cell therapy has been utilized in the treatment of periodontitis. Recent studies have demonstrated that treatment with apoptotic mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibits immunomodulatory effects comparable to those of living MSCs. However, the effect of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) on the efficacy of apoptotic MSCs therapy for periodontitis remains poorly understood.

pmc-13231324.title: Trends in antifungal use characteristics in primary care in Spain, 2019 to 2024: a nationwide study
pmc-13231324.creator: Álvaro Solaz-García, Héctor Sánchez-Herrero, Nerea Valles-Murcia, María José Soriano-Ortega, Alba Ruiz-Gaitán
pmc-13231324.description: BackgroundAntifungal resistance is a growing global concern in the context of antimicrobial resistance. Although primary care is the main setting for managing superficial fungal infections, national evidence on antifungal consumption in Spain remains limited. This study analyzes the characteristics of antifungal use in Spanish primary care.

pmc-13316306.title: Chronic viral infection aggravates white adipose tissue dysfunction and liver pathology in obesity
pmc-13316306.creator: Katarzyna M Luda, Marianne Agerholm, Si Brask Sonne, Dipsikha Biswas, Lisa DeCamp, Russell G Jones, Allan Randrup Thomsen, Benjamin Anderschou Holbeck Jensen, Jan Pravsgaard Christensen, Kei Sakamoto
pmc-13316306.description: BackgroundWhite adipose tissue (WAT) plays a central role in maintaining systemic metabolic homeostasis by buffering lipid flux throughout the body. Impairment of this lipid-buffering capacity is a hallmark of obesity and has also been observed during chronic viral infection. Such dysfunction is closely associated with ectopic fat accumulation, particularly in the liver.

pmc-13640782.title: De novo design of autocatalytically forming intra- and intermolecular isopeptide bonds to construct rigid covalent protein assemblies
pmc-13640782.creator: Lukas F Milles, Evelyn B Huddy, Ann Carr, Yang Hsia, Xinting Li, Alex Kang, Banumathi Sankaran, Asim K. Bera, David Baker
pmc-13640782.description: Isopeptide bonds are amide bonds between amino acid side chains that can form autocatalytically, notably in the pili of Gram-positive bacteria. Here, we design de novo proteins that form both intramolecular and intermolecular isopeptide bonds entirely autocatalytically. We report over 50 designs that form isopeptide bonds, validated by mass spectrometry and 5 crystal structures.
